Assess Quasi-Identifier Re-Identification Risk (k-Anonymity & l-Diversity)

Source: R/anonymity.R
assess_reidentification_risk.Rd

Audits an extracted or clinical data frame across user-specified quasi-identifiers (for example age_band, zip3, gender, site) to quantify $k$-anonymity compliance, prosecutor and journalist re-identification risks, sample uniqueness, and optional distinct $l$-diversity for a sensitive outcome column. Equivalence class diagnostics use opaque integer class IDs and aggregate counts only—never logging raw participant records.

Usage

assess_reidentification_risk(
  data,
  quasi_ids,
  k_min = 5L,
  sensitive_col = NULL,
  l_min = 2L,
  sampling_fraction = 1,
  include_na = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble to audit.

quasi_ids

Character vector of one or more quasi-identifier column names present in data.

k_min

Integer minimum required equivalence class size (must be >= 2L, default 5L).

sensitive_col

Optional character scalar name of a sensitive outcome column in data for distinct $l$-diversity auditing.

l_min

Integer minimum required number of distinct non-NA values of sensitive_col within every equivalence class (must be >= 2L, default 2L). Ignored when sensitive_col = NULL.

sampling_fraction

Numeric population sampling fraction in (0, 1] used to compute conservative journalist re-identification risk upper bounds (min(1, sampling_fraction / k)). Defaults to 1 (conservative full-population / census upper bound equal to prosecutor risk).

include_na

Logical scalar; if TRUE (default), NA values in quasi_ids form their own equivalence category ("<NA>"). If FALSE, rows containing NA in any quasi-identifier are excluded from equivalence class grouping and reported in n_rows_excluded_na.

Value

An S3 object of class "airgap_reid_risk" containing:

  • n_rows, n_rows_evaluated, n_rows_excluded_na, n_classes

  • quasi_ids, k_min, min_k, median_k

  • n_unique_rows, pct_unique_rows

  • n_violating_classes, n_violating_rows, pct_violating_rows

  • passes_k_anonymity (logical)

  • prosecutor_risk_max, prosecutor_risk_mean

  • journalist_risk_max, journalist_risk_mean, sampling_fraction

  • sensitive_col, l_min, min_l, n_l_violating_classes, n_l_violating_rows, pct_l_violating_rows, passes_l_diversity

  • equivalence_classes: privacy-safe tibble indexed by opaque class_id

  • row_class_size: integer vector of class sizes aligned to data rows

  • row_violates: logical vector flagging rows failing $k$-anonymity (or $l$-diversity when sensitive_col is supplied)

Examples

df <- tibble::tibble(
  site = c(rep("North", 6), rep("South", 2), rep("West", 5)),
  wave = c(rep(1L, 6), rep(2L, 2), rep(1L, 5)),
  diagnosis = c("A", "B", "A", "B", "C", "A", "A", "A", "B", "C", "B", "C", "A")
)
assess_reidentification_risk(df, quasi_ids = c("site", "wave"),
                             k_min = 5L, sensitive_col = "diagnosis", l_min = 2L)
#> <airgap_reid_risk> [k-anonymity (k>=5): FAIL]
#>   Quasi-identifiers:   site, wave
#>   Rows evaluated:      13 / 13 across 3 equivalence class(es)
#>   Min / Median k:      2 / 5
#>   Sample uniques (k=1):0 (0%)
#>   Rows with k < 5:     2 (15.38%)
#>   Prosecutor risk:     max=0.5000 | mean=0.2308
#>   Journalist risk:     max=0.5000 | mean=0.2308 (f=1)
#>   l-diversity ('diagnosis', l>=2): FAIL (min_l=1, violating rows=2 [15.38%])
